jobs.title: Sports Medicine, Clinical Assistant Professor, Orthopaedics, Sports Medicine
jobs.description: The Clinical Assistant Professor should be prepared to contribute to the academic and clinical missions of the department, participating in resident medical student, and undergraduate training and education. This university based full-time academic faculty position requires Level 1 Hand Call, participation in resident/fellow didactics, and reserach mentorship for young learners.

jobs.title: Professor (All Ranks) in AI-Human Collaboration
jobs.institution: Arizona State University: The Polytechnic School
jobs.description:
The Ira A. Fulton Schools of Engineering at Arizona State University (ASU) and The Polytechnic School (TPS) seek applicants for an open-rank, tenure-track or tenured faculty position in AI-human collaboration. TPS, one of the eight Fulton Schools, has a vibrant scholarly community conducting fundamental and applied research (learn more at https://research.engineering.asu.edu/). We are seeking applicants who can strengthen our research and educational efforts in human-enriching technologies. The applicant’s scholarship in this area may apply to medical human factors, defense, user experience, learning engineering, aviation, training and education, or another relevant area.
We search for applicants who will contribute to our academic programs, promote transdisciplinary teaching and research, and help the University achieve its aspirations, including enabling student success, transforming society, valuing entrepreneurship, and conducting use-inspired AI research. Faculty in the Human Systems Engineering (HSE) program at TPS combine psychology and engineering to design systems consistent with human strengths and limitations, creating technology that works for humans, and currently have expertise in applied cognition, human-technology interaction, AI-human teaming, learning, and more. Multiple affiliated centers are available for collaboration and support, such as the Center for Innovation in Healthy and Resilient Aging, the Center for Accelerating Operational Efficiency for Homeland Security, the Center for Human, Artificial Intelligence, and Robot Teaming (CHART) in the Global Security Initiative, and the Learning Engineering Institute. Faculty members in the Fulton Schools are expected to develop an internationally recognized, externally funded research program; adopt effective pedagogical practices in developing and delivering graduate and undergraduate courses in their respective Fulton Engineering School; advise undergraduate and graduate student research and projects; and undertake service activities.
Appointments will be at the Assistant, Associate, or (full) Professor rank commensurate with the candidate’s experience and accomplishments, beginning August 2027.
Essential Functions
Contribute to curriculum development
Deliver instruction in-person and/or online
Supervise honors, master’s, and doctoral students
Conduct research publishable in top-tier journals and/or conferences in the discipline
Develop grant proposals for external funding as PI or co-PI
Participate in professional and internal service

jobs.title: Associate Professor, Endowed Chair in Community Practice
jobs.institution: Johns Hopkins University: School of Education
jobs.description:
The Johns Hopkins University School of Education seeks candidates for a tenure-eligible Associate Professor in Community Practice, with an emphasis in Early Childhood Education (through grade 3). The position is intended to advance the translation of scientific, evidence-based methods into practice for teachers and community practitioners, with the goal of improving the quality of education for all students. The successful candidate will bring an established research program and a demonstrated record of leadership to this work, along with a sustained scholarly commitment to early childhood as a foundational period of human development. This position offers the opportunity to shape graduate education and lead partnerships that connect research to real-world practice in early learning, underserved, and urban communities across diverse local, national, and global contexts. Qualified candidates will be considered for eligibility for a new endowed chair, called the William and Sylvia Cohen Associate Professor in Community Practice.
Responsibilities:
CURRICULUM AND TEACHING
Evaluate, develop, and deliver curricula for JHU School of Education degree programs that translate advances in learning, technology, and instruction science into practice accessible to pre- and in-service teachers and community practitioners.
Mentor master's and doctoral degree candidates to deepen their understanding of early childhood as the critical period shaping a child's physical, intellectual, emotional, and social development, as well as language acquisition, and provide senior guidance on dissertation research in this area.
Engage in service to the department, school, and profession appropriate to rank.
Research and Evidence Building
Strengthen the evidence base on what makes educational programs and initiatives effective, with particular attention to early learners and underserved and urban populations.
Collaborate with, and where appropriate lead, experts in teaching and learning, brain and language development, and child development across Johns Hopkins University with a specific interest in early childhood development.
Collaborate with faculty across units and centers on interdisciplinary research and grant activity.
Hold a secondary affiliation with one or more of the School of Education’s five Research Centers: https://education.jhu.edu/faculty-research/centers-institutes/
Community and Partnership Engagement
Build and sustain partnerships with schools and communities that bridge the gap between cutting-edge research and everyday practice, working toward improved educational outcomes for students.
Work directly with community stakeholders to design and implement practical programs and technologies that support student performance and long-term outcomes and help secure the funding and institutional support these partnerships require.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor Tenure-Track Positions in AI for Science for Fall 2027, Courant Institute School of Mathematics, Computing, and Data Science
jobs.institution: New York University: Center for Data Science
jobs.description:
The Courant Institute School of Mathematics, Computing, and Data Science at New York University seeks candidates for four (4) assistant professor faculty positions, anticipated to begin in September 2027. Faculty members are expected to be outstanding scholars and to participate in teaching at all levels, from undergraduate to doctoral. The aim of this position is to expand in the area of ML/AI for science, with a particular focus on the physical sciences, chemistry, biology, and areas of relevance for the Mind Brain Machines initiative. The ideal candidate will be firmly engaged in computational science, AI methodology, and scientific applications.
These positions are based in the Center for Data Science and may include affiliations with the relevant departments in NYU’s Arts & Science, or the Tandon School of Engineering.
The Courant Institute School of Mathematics, Computing, and Data Science furthers NYU’s longtime preeminence in mathematics, applied mathematics, data science, computer science, and engineering. The school includes the Department of Mathematics, the Center for Data Science, and the Department of Computer Science.
In compliance with NYC's Pay Transparency Act, the annual base salary range for this position is $110,000 - $160,000. New York University considers factors such as (but not limited to) the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate's work experience, education/training, key skills, and internal peer equity, as well as market and organization considerations.
For full consideration, applications should be submitted by Jan 8, 2027. Applications will be considered until the positions are filled.

jobs.title: Environmental Engineering Faculty Position
jobs.institution: Vanderbilt University: Civil and Environmental Engineering
jobs.description:
The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering (CEE) at Vanderbilt University invites applications for a faculty position in environmental engineering beginning Fall 2027. The successful candidate is expected to have an established track record in research and education and will be hired at the associate or full professor level (depending on the record, experience, and qualifications).
The Department seeks candidates with expertise in nuclear environmental engineering, broadly defined to encompass environmental challenges associated with current and emerging nuclear technologies. Areas of interest include, but are not limited to, environmental impacts, sustainability, safety and management across the nuclear energy life cycle, advanced nuclear energy systems and fuel cycles, with applications to power (for civilian and/or military use), radioactive waste treatment, storage, transport and disposal, facility and site decontamination, decommissioning and remediation, environmental monitoring and characterization, risk assessment, and safeguards and security. Research employing experimental, computational, theoretical, or data-driven approaches is of interest.
This position is part of the School of Engineering’s commitment to establishing an interdisciplinary Defense Technology Cluster aimed at addressing related grand societal and scientific challenges. This hiring focus reflects our dedication to strengthening collaboration across disciplines within the School of Engineering and the University.
The successful candidate is expected to leverage and be closely affiliated with on-going research initiative and centers at Vanderbilt University such as the Consortium for Risk Evaluation with Stakeholder Participation (CRESP; nuclear energy systems and waste management, nuclear missions, nuclear fuel cycles and associated waste management); Vanderbilt Center for Sustainability, Energy and Climate (energy integration, resource sustainability, climate adaptation and mitigation, and systems risk, reliability and resilience); and Institute for National Security (interdisciplinary security research, experiential education, defense innovation, and cross-sector collaboration). The successful candidates will be expected to adopt Vanderbilt’s “radical collaboration” concept and leverage resources and expertise that exist within the School of Engineering, as well as the University as a whole.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor (Tenure Track), Hydrodynamic Modeling
jobs.institution: Stony Brook University: Division of Marine Sciences
jobs.description:
Description of Duties:
The School of Marine and Atmospheric Sciences (SoMAS) at Stony Brook University invites applications for assistant professor in Marine Sciences. Candidates in the areas of coastal or estuarine circulation modeling, high-resolution or adaptive-scale modeling, air-sea coupled modeling, natural hazard modeling, coupled physical-biogeochemical modeling, coupled biophysical modeling, sediment transport modeling, large-eddy simulations, and approaches that integrate hydrodynamic and statistical analyses to understand variability, and extremes in coastal dynamics are especially encouraged to apply.
The successful candidate will have a strong commitment to undergraduate and graduate teaching, and the ability to establish and sustain an externally funded research program. SoMAS is a multi-disciplinary environment, with opportunity for collaboration within the School to advance its research mission.
Special Notes: This is a tenure track position. FLSA Exempt position, not eligible for the overtime provisions of the FLSA.
Campus Description:
Stony Brook University, home to many highly ranked graduate research programs, is located 60 miles from New York City on Long Island's scenic North Shore. Our 1,100-acre campus is home to 24,000 undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral students and more than 13,500 faculty and staff. SBU is a comprehensive research-intensive university and a member of the prestigious Association of American Universities (AAU), which includes 34 public universities among its 62 members. SBU consists of 12 schools and colleges and a teaching hospital that provides state-of-the-art healthcare in the Long Island region. SBU also manages and performs joint research with Brookhaven National Laboratory, the only Department of Energy Laboratory in the Northeast, and hosts the Institute for Advanced Computational Sciences that maintains high performance computational resources and engages faculty from across campus. SBU is also the anchor institution for the NY Climate Exchange and organizes on-campus environmental research initiatives, such as the Collaborative for the Earth. SBU sustains an international reputation that cuts across the arts, humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences, through programs such as the Emerson String Quartet, the Pollock-Krasner House in East Hampton, New York, the Humanities Institute, and the Southampton Arts Program.
School of Marine, Atmospheric, and Sustainability Sciences: The School of Marine, Atmospheric, and Sustainability Sciences (SoMAS) is the State University of New York's center for marine and atmospheric research, education, and public service. It has access to state of the art research facilities, including a fleet of research vessels, the Southampton Marine Science Station, and seawater labs at Flax Pond Marine Lab. Approximately 800 graduate and undergraduate students currently work and study at SoMAS. The SoMAS Faculty are internationally known for their leadership in research in atmospheric sciences, all the major disciplines of oceanography – biological, chemical, geological, and physical – and sustainability studies. http://www.somas.stonybrook.edu

jobs.title: Open Rank Thoracic Surgeon
jobs.description:
The Department of Surgery, Division of Thoracic Surgery at the University of Virginia seeks candidates for an open rank and track Thoracic Surgeon. Rank and tenure status are dependent upon qualifications and experience. The ideal candidate should have experience in the surgical management of all aspects of general thoracic surgery including lung transplantation. The successful candidate will have an interest in lung transplantation and minimally-invasive/robotic thoracic surgical procedures with a desire to expand these programs. An esophageal disease interest would be considered a plus.
Job Duties:
Teaching - Teaching encompasses all activities that directly facilitate student and resident education, including weekly attendance and participation in teaching conferences, periodic lectures and ward teaching for students and residents, completion of evaluations. Resident teaching is of great importance to our program and culture here at UVA.
Research - The research component includes scholarly publication, presenting at academic conferences and submitting grants.
Service - University service involves membership and participation in departmental, hospital, and School of Medicine committees, attending departmental meetings, thoracic tumor board, division meetings, resident recruitment and interviews, timely completion of medical records, answering email, taking an equal share of on call time, and clinic visits.
In addition to the above job responsibilities, other duties may be assigned.
The University of Virginia Health System is located in Charlottesville, Virginia, which boasts abundant recreational activities and easy access to the Blue Ridge Mountains, the eastern shore and the nation's capital.
This position will be open to applications until filled. For additional information regarding the position, please contact Linda Martin, MD, MPH, Chief of Thoracic Surgery, Professor of Surgery via e-mail LM6YB@uvahealth.org.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Economics and Computational Social Science, Tenure-Track
jobs.institution: New York University: AD_Computational Social Science
jobs.description:
The Division of Social Science at New York University Abu Dhabi (NYUAD) is inviting applications for a tenure-track position in Economics and Data Science. The successful candidate’s tenure home would be in the Economics program and will hold an affiliation in the new MSc in Interdisciplinary Data Science and AI (MIDSAI). The position carries a teaching load of three courses per year, one of which will be for MIDSAI.
As NYUAD is a research university, we seek applicants with an active research agenda in economics and AI. The ideal candidate will be a leader in applying data science and AI tools to questions in economics, or conducting empirical research on the economic implications of AI. This specialization is broadly construed and might include research related to big data collection, machine learning, natural language processing, image or video analysis, network inference, computational finance, online platforms and algorithmic behavior, and more. We are especially interested in scholars who work effectively in multidisciplinary teams and environments. All candidates should demonstrate important contributions to their area of research.
About NYU Abu Dhabi
https://nyuad.nyu.edu/en/
NYU Abu Dhabi is the first comprehensive liberal arts and research campus in the Middle East to be operated abroad by a major American research university. Times Higher Education ranks NYU among the top 30 universities in the world, making NYU Abu Dhabi the highest-ranked university in the UAE and MENA region. NYU Abu Dhabi has integrated a highly selective undergraduate curriculum across the disciplines with a world center for advanced research and scholarship. The university enables its students in the sciences, engineering, social sciences, humanities, and arts to succeed in an increasingly interdependent world and advance cooperation and progress on humanity’s shared challenges. NYU Abu Dhabi’s high-achieving students have come from over 120 countries and speak over 100 languages. Together, NYU's campuses in New York, Abu Dhabi, and Shanghai form the backbone of a unique global university, giving faculty and students opportunities to experience varied learning environments and immersion in other cultures at one or more of the numerous study-abroad sites NYU maintains on six continents.
NYUAD is committed to upholding a culture of non-discrimination, anti-harassment, dignity, and mutual respect; providing equal access and opportunity; and fostering academic excellence in learning, research, and teaching.
Students are drawn from among the world’s best. They are bright, intellectually passionate, and committed to building a campus environment anchored in mutual respect, understanding, and care. The NYUAD undergraduate student body has garnered an impressive record of scholarships, graduate-school admissions, and other global honors. Graduate education is an area of growth for the University; the current graduate student population of over 100 students is expected to expand in the next decade as doctoral programs are developed.
Working for NYUAD
At NYUAD, we recognize that Abu Dhabi is more than where you work; it’s your home. In order for faculty/academic staff to thrive, we offer a comprehensive benefits package. This starts with a generous relocation allowance; educational assistance for your dependents; access to health and wellness services; and more. NYUAD is committed to faculty/academic staff success throughout the academic trajectory, providing support for ambitious and world-class research projects and innovative, interactive teaching approaches. Support for dual-career families is a priority. Visit our website for more information on benefits for you and your dependents.

jobs.title: 2027 Actuarial Science Tenure-Track Assistant/Associate Professor
jobs.description:
Wenzhou-Kean University (WKU), located in Wenzhou, China, one of three Sino-American universities along with NYU Shanghai and Duke Kunshan University, is approved by the Ministry of Education of China. Launched in 2012, WKU offers a unique model of higher education in partnership with Kean University, a comprehensive, public university in the state of New Jersey that is accredited by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education.
WKU sits on approximately 500 beautiful acres and currently enrolls about 5,500 undergraduate and graduate students, and it is now in the midst of a rapid growth that will bring enrollment to 7,000 students within the next three years. All instruction is in English, and all curriculum is provided by Kean University.
In addition to its current 18 undergraduate programs, WKU has been approved by the Ministry of Education for offering 14 Master’s and 3 doctorate programs. WKU highly values research-powered teaching and learning, and the average number of faculty publications and the Field-weighted Citation Impact are among the best of leading Chinese academic institutions.
Wenzhou is one of the most vibrant and economically advanced developed cities on China’s East Coast, located one hour by plane and three hours by high-speed train from Shanghai.
About the Job:
The College of Science, Mathematics, and Technology is seeking highly motivated individuals in Actuarial Science to join the mathematical sciences department at WKU.
All faculty positions are full-time assignments, effective for the start of the 2027 Spring or the 2027 Fall semester. These positions are full-time assignments appointed on a 3-year contract at the first instance and are renewable upon successful reappointment review.
A Tenure-track Assistant/Associate Professor is a full-time, 10-month employee who teaches 24 credits per academic year. Tenure-track faculty normally teach 2 different courses with each section consisting typically of 24-30 students. Faculty is required to conduct research, provide high quality teaching and provide service to the university and/or professional community. Six credits teaching release time will be provided to new faculty each year for the first three consecutive years of the appointment to support external research grant development and other significant research endeavors. Thereafter, release time may be available by application on competitive basis. The university will provide start-up grants (up to 300,000 RMB) in support of their research programs. After joining WKU, faculty will apply to a variety of internal research funds and external grants at the municipal, provincial, and national levels. Faculty members successfully obtaining eligible external grants will be afforded release time ranging from 3-12 credits per year. Tenure-track faculty are also expected to provide service to the university and/or professional community.
Teaching assignments and related responsibilities may include day, evening, and online courses. Interest or experience in using advanced instructional technologies to improve the teaching/learning process is highly desirable. All faculty may be required to teach General Education courses as needed. Opportunities are also available to teach disciplinary support courses.
Faculty positions at WKU offer:
$70,000-$77,000 for Assistant Professors. The salary of extraordinary candidates shall be determined on a case-by-case basis.
The University will provide start-up grants to support tenure-track faculty to start their research programs
A well-rounded healthcare coverage, housing options and subsidy up to $3,000, home traveling up to $6,000 (2 international round-trip airfares), a reimbursement to cover relocation expenses up to $1,000 and shuttle bus to campus for work.
The university provides financial assistance for academic travel.
WKU tuition waiver up to 50% for spouse/dependent children of faculty for undergraduate programs
The opportunity to teach high-quality students. About 60% of graduates who pursued graduate study have been admitted to graduate schools at the World’s Top 50 Universities, and more than 80% of graduates who pursued graduate study at the World’s Top 100 Universities.

jobs.title: Faculty Position in HEALTH SERVICES RESEARCH/HEALTH POLICY
jobs.institution: University of Michigan-Ann Arbor: School of Public Health
jobs.description: The Department of Health Management & Policy (HMP) at the University of Michigan is seeking a tenure-track faculty member at the assistant or advanced assistant level—with expertise in the fields of health services research and health policy. Individuals who have or will complete degrees in health services research or health policy, or related fields with a focus on health services such as healthcare management, health services organizations, health services quality and implementation, and related areas are encouraged to apply. With a start date of August 2027, the candidate must have completed a PhD by September 1, 2027.

jobs.title: Artist Faculty in Trombone
jobs.description:
Position Description
The Department of Music at Stony Brook seeks a trombonist with an exemplary reputation; profound understanding of their craft; strong ability to communicate their vision; well versed in the solo, chamber music, and orchestral literature. The appointee will be an excellent trombonist in the performance of classical music, with a deep knowledge of, and commitment to, the music of our time and skill in its performance. We seek a trombonist who will successfully recruit and teach trombone students on the masters and doctoral levels, and who will coach chamber and brass ensemble music. The appointee will be open-minded, inspirational, and dedicated, and serve as a mentor to their students while having a positive effect on the Department of Music community.

jobs.title: Assistant or Associate Professor of Nephrology
jobs.institution: Howard University College of Medicine: Nephrology
jobs.description:
The Division of Nephrology at Howard University College of Medicine invites applications for a full-time faculty position at the Assistant or Associate Professor level, on the tenure track or clinician-educator track. We seek a nephrologist to provide inpatient and outpatient kidney care and to teach residents and fellows. The role offers strong opportunities to lead in kidney disease prevention, home and in-center dialysis care, and research on the genetic and social determinants of kidney health, including APOL1.
Candidates with interests in CKD prevention, home dialysis, transplant access, glomerular disease, or kidney health equity are especially encouraged to apply.
Primary Responsibilities
Clinical Care
Provide inpatient nephrology consultation and outpatient chronic kidney disease care, and participate in the nephrology call schedule.
Manage patients on hemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis, and continuous kidney replacement therapy, serving as dialysis unit attending as assigned.
Contribute to programs in CKD prevention, home dialysis, or transplant referral and access.
Teaching and Education
Teach and supervise medical students, internal medicine residents, and nephrology fellows in clinic, dialysis, and inpatient settings.
Contribute to fellowship didactics, conferences, and the internal medicine clerkship curriculum.
Advise and mentor trainees in clinical and scholarly work.
Research and Scholarship
Pursue clinical, translational, or health services research in kidney disease and kidney health equity.
Publish peer-reviewed scholarship and participate in clinical trials and registries.
Academic Service
Serve on division, department, hospital, College, and University committees.
Contribute to the clinical, educational, research, and service missions of Howard University.

jobs.title: Associate or Assistant Professor of Physiology and Biophysics, Basic Science Educator Track
jobs.institution: Howard University College of Medicine: Physiology and Biophysics
jobs.description:
The Department of Physiology and Biophysics at Howard University College of Medicine invites applications for a faculty position at the Instructor or Assistant Professor level on the Basic Science Educator Track, a non-tenure track for faculty whose primary focus is teaching. We seek an educator who brings proficiency and enthusiasm for teaching physiology to medical students. The successful candidate will teach systems physiology, contribute to curriculum development, and participate in student advising and mentoring.
Basic Science Educator Track appointments are renewable term appointments. Initial appointments are for two years, with renewable terms of up to five years.
Primary Responsibilities
Teaching
Teach systems physiology to medical students through lectures, small-group discussions, case-based instruction, and other active-learning approaches, with opportunities to teach dental, allied health, and graduate students.
Integrate physiologic principles with clinical correlations across organ systems.
Use innovative, active-learning teaching methods, including simulation and physiology laboratory exercises, to engage students.
Assess and evaluate student performance, including writing examination items aligned with USMLE content expectations.
Curriculum Development
Collaborate on the design of an integrated, systems-based pre-clerkship curriculum.
Update instructional materials to reflect advances in physiology and their clinical applications.
Advising and Mentoring
Provide academic advising to medical students.
Mentor students in scholarly projects and professional development.
Scholarship
Faculty are encouraged to participate in educational scholarship, curriculum innovation, and professional development activities, as appropriate to their appointment and teaching responsibilities. Scholarly presentations and publications are encouraged but are not required unless specified by the approved faculty track and promotion criteria.
Academic Service
Participate in departmental and College meetings, educational committees, student admissions activities, and other academic service responsibilities, as appropriate to the faculty appointment.
Contribute to community and outreach activities, including pipeline programs for future health professionals.

jobs.title: Open-Rank Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor of Instruction in Electrical Engineering
jobs.institution: Columbia University in the City of New York: Electrical Engineering
jobs.description:
The Department of Electrical Engineering (EE) at Columbia University welcomes applications for a full-time, open-rank Professor of Instruction position. This will be a non-tenured position that can be appointed at the Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor of Instruction rank. This newly created faculty position reflects the department's commitment to teaching excellence and the continued development of its electrical engineering curriculum.
The successful candidate will be expected to teach broadly across the electrical engineering curriculum, with the majority of their teaching focused on signal processing and communications. The position places particular emphasis on undergraduate education, including delivering high-quality instruction, mentoring and advising students, and contributing to course and curriculum development. The successful candidate will also be expected to undertake departmental service and administrative responsibilities, participate in educational initiatives, supervising capstone projects, as well engaging with student activities and organizations.
This position offers an opportunity to play a significant role in shaping undergraduate electrical engineering education at Columbia.

jobs.title: Artist Faculty in Guitar
jobs.description:
Position Description:
The Department of Music seeks a guitar instructor to serve as part-time artist-in-residence, teaching guitar performance to advanced undergraduates and graduate students in the MM and DMA programs and supervising the teaching of undergrads. Applicants should have a stellar reputation as a performer, profound understanding of their craft, and experience teaching advanced students. Appointee will be expected to have a deep knowledge of the entire classical guitar repertoire from the Renaissance through music of the 20th and 21st centuries, as well as a strong interest in electric guitar. Additional fields of interest will align with the College of Arts and Sciences vision of interdisciplinary initiatives and can include Jazz, popular music, improvisation, historical guitar, theorbo, and Latin American as well as other styles of music. Appointee should also demonstrate a strong commitment to diversity in their recruiting efforts.
Responsibilities:
Faculty will teach weekly acoustic guitar and/or electric guitar lessons to advanced undergraduate and graduate students throughout the academic year, give regular studio classes, sit on audition panels and juries, and be available for chamber music coaching. A strong academic background is desired as the appointee will also help to prepare students for lecture recitals on guitar and participate in the supervision of students’ doctoral work.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor- Child Clinical Psychologist
jobs.description:
The Yale Child Study Center’s Clinical Services are comprised of a multidisciplinary faculty and a number of training programs, including psychology practicum, internship, and post-doctoral fellowship. Our services include child and adult treatment, home-based services, and assessment services. Psychoeducational testing, developmental evaluations, and team evaluations are an important part of our array of services. The Child Study Center is committed to recruiting and supporting clinicians, researchers, and leaders representing diverse backgrounds today, as well as those in succeeding generations in the service of its clinical, research, training, policy, and prevention agendas. Yale Child Study Center Clinical Services has an opening for full-time child psychologist dedicated to providing evaluation and treatment services to young children and their families. The successful candidate will be appointed as an Assistant Professor of Child Psychology on the Academic Clinician ladder track. A primary focus of this position is to provide developmental assessment and evidence-based treatment for children under ten and their families. Additional job responsbilities include:
· Conducting developmental and psychological assessments of children and adolescents
· Providing evidence-based treatment to children and their caregivers, with a special emphasis on services for children aged 10 and younger and their families.
· Providing Child Parent Psychotherapy (CPP) to young children who have experienced traumatic events
· Collaborating with members of clinical teams to inform comprehensive care plans
· Participation in the psychology training faculty, including training and supervision of practicum students, psychology interns through the Yale Child Study Center’s APA-accredited internship, and/or post-doctoral fellows on the pediatric psychology track
While not required on the Academic Clinician track, research and quality improvement projects are available and encouraged as part of a collaborative team.
The salary ranges listed below reflect the anticipated compensation range for all ranks included in this recruitment.
$125,000-$150,000

jobs.title: Faculty Position in Experimental Condensed Matter Physics 2026
jobs.description:
Carnegie Mellon University invites applications for a tenure-track position in experimental condensed matter physics. This position is part of a planned expansion in quantum materials and devices that is coordinated with the Department of Materials Science & Engineering. This includes a plan for multiple hires, shared equipment/facilities, and other resources in order to integrate expertise in understanding the physics of, synthesizing, and characterizing quantum materials to enable their use in real devices. The successful candidate should demonstrate a strong independent research program that brings synergy with experimentalists and theorists in the Department of Physics and the Department of Materials Science & Engineering who work in the area of quantum materials and devices.
The appointment is intended to be at the Assistant Professor level, but exceptional candidates at the Associate Professor or Professor level may be considered.
The successful candidate will benefit from regional quantum science initiatives via the Pittsburgh Quantum Institute (PQI) and from exceptional local facilities, such as the Bertucci Nanotechnology Laboratory, the Materials Characterization Facility, and the Western Pennsylvania Quantum Information Core (WP-QIC).
The successful candidate will arrive at a moment of major new investment and opportunity at Carnegie Mellon. Ken Griffin's recent gift of more than $3 billion comprises a $500 million investment in the Kenneth C. Griffin School of Computer Science, $500 million to support other initiatives on the Pittsburgh campus, and $2 billion to establish CMU Miami, a new campus designed around interdisciplinary research and major scientific and societal challenges. We seek candidates who will actively engage in interdisciplinary research on the Pittsburgh campus while identifying opportunities on the Miami campus as well.

jobs.title: FA27-044: Assistant Professor, Electrical and Computer Engineering
jobs.institution: Southern Illinois University Edwardsville: Electrical and Computer Engineering
jobs.description:
The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Southern Illinois University Edwardsville (SIUE) is seeking to fill a tenure-track faculty position at the Assistant Professor level. The Department maintains undergraduate programs in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, and Mechatronics and Robotics Engineering. It also maintains an M.S. program in Electrical and Computer Engineering.
The primary responsibilities of this person will be to support the Mechatronics and Robotics Engineering program, including teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in control systems, power systems, or related areas.
SIUE is a strong advocate of the teacher-scholar model, and therefore, the successful candidate is expected to be active in the design and teaching of classes that have extensive project-based learning activities, publish scholarly work, promote undergraduate research, supervise and mentor graduate students, and participate in service activities. The selected candidate will also be expected to establish and sustain an externally funded research program in a related area.
The School of Engineering is committed to attracting, supporting, and retaining employees with all identities and backgrounds, and particularly candidates form underrepresented groups in STEM such as women faculty and faculty of color. SIUE faculty are encouraged to contribute to inclusive excellence in both the academic community and region through research, teaching, and service.
Southern Illinois University Edwardsville nurtures an open, respectful, and welcoming climate that facilitates learning and work. SIUE is committed to education that explores the historic significance of diversity in order to understand the present and to better enable our community to engage the future. Integral to this commitment, Southern Illinois University Edwardsville strives for a student body and a workforce that is both diverse and inclusive. We strongly encourage candidates from historically underrepresented groups, including women, members of racially minoritized groups, and individuals with disabilities, to apply. For more on our State of Diversity, visit SIUE Mission, Goals and Plans.
